They Bought a Lexus LC for $123,494, Put It Up for Sale Immediately, Refused $163,500
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Yeah, it’s not a clickbait story, as this actually happened, and if you are curious whether the Lexus LC in question is still for sale, then the answer is yes, and it’s a brand new car.
The seller reportedly bought it new in September 2026 and refrained from driving it. Therefore, this machine has only 20 miles (30 km) on the clock. The selling price was $123,494, as per the window stick attached in the gallery, and the owner believes that the vehicle is worth more than $163,500. That’s because he refused to sell it for the latter sum at an online auction that recently ended.
This 2026 Lexus LC 500 Inspiration Series Coupe was advertised on Cars&Bids. The gavel hit the table on November 4, 2026, and the premium grand tourer failed to change hands, even if it would have made its owner a nice profit of $40,000. The model is worth between $140,000 and over $175,000 in today’s market, and it’s up for you to decide whether the seller is being greedy or if they might make even more money from parting ways with their brand new LC.
The car is finished in Smoke Matte Gray and has a white and black cockpit. It rides on 21-inch forged wheels, has active rear-wheel steering, a limited-slip differential, and a carbon fiber roof. Additional features mentioned in the ad include the head-up display, leather upholstery, heated and ventilated seats at the front, a Mark Levinson premium sound system, and the Lexus Safety System+ 2.5 bundle of driving assistance gizmos.
Photo: Cars&Bids Power is supplied by a V8 engine, and it is a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter unit, in case you forgot. The Lexus LC 500 had 471 horsepower in this configuration, which translates to 477 metric horsepower and 351 kilowatts, and 398 lb-ft (540 Nm) of torque. A ten-speed automatic transmission deploys everything to the rear axle.
Mind you, this model is not exactly a dragster disguised as a comfortable and very good-looking premium grand tourer, but it won’t make a fool of itself either in a straight-line acceleration. That’s because it needs 4.4 seconds to zip from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). The convertible is two-tenths of a second slower. And the standing quarter mile takes over 13 seconds, with an exit speed of 110 mph (175 kph).
This paragraph would normally be dedicated to the known flaws, but since the 2026 Lexus LC 500 Inspiration Series Coupe in question has only 20 miles under its belt, it is a brand new vehicle with no issues. It has a clean Carfax history report, a clean Virginia title, and is located in Centreville, VA. By the way, due to the fact that it is new, it hasn’t required any servicing yet. And there are no modifications on deck, not even tinted windows, or a paint protection film.
In addition to the car, the next owner will get two key fobs, one wallet key, the owner’s manuals, and the window sticker. Thus, if you want one of these in your life and are willing to get it at a very steep premium compared to what it initially cost, then you should get in touch with the seller and make an offer. But whatever you do, you should know that they likely won’t accept anything under $163,500.
Photo: Cars&Bids We’d want to know how much the seller hopes to get from parting ways with their new Lexus LC 500 Inspiration Series Coupe from the 2026 model year, but your guess is as good as ours. And to be honest, we would not be surprised to learn that they might try to get very close to the $200,000 mark. After all, that’s what some dealers are doing.
Now, if you were really shopping for a fresh Lexus LC 500 in the Inspiration Series configuration with a fixed-roof design and the model sat at the very top of your shopping list, would you really try to get this example knowing that its first and only owner refused to let it go for $163,500? If you said yes, then you may want to reach out to them here on Cars&Bids and discuss the details. And if you end up buying it, then feel free to tell us what you paid for it.
In the meantime, we will remind you that Lexus pulled the plug on the LC a few months ago. Production of this model ended in August 2026, as that is when the final copy rolled off the assembly line at the Motomachi (Toyota City) factory in Japan, a little over 9 years after it entered production.
The LC was based on the TNGA-L platform, shared with the Lexus LS, the Toyota Crown Sedan, and the Mirai, and was offered as a two-door coupe and a two-door convertible. Besides the V8 engine, customers could also get it with a hybridized gasoline engine. The electrified 3.5L V6 made 354 hp and 350 lb-ft (475 Nm) of torque, enabling 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds.
